name: Dawat Restaurant (Indus Lodges)
must_try: Grilled river trout / mixed BBQ platter
pros: Rooftop with panoramic river-and-mountain views
Generous family BBQ platters and fresh trout
Attentive service, tourist and local favorite
cons: Small Tripadvisor sample (30) vs strong Google base
take: Still the standout special-occasion rooftop in Gilgit; trout and BBQ are the reason to come.

name: Gilgit Food Yard
area: River View Rd (opp. ETI office), Gilgit
pros: Riverside outdoor seating with mountain backdrop
Reputedly best chapli kebab in town, plus wild trout and mantu
Fair prices for the setting
cons: Can get crowded and slow at dinner peak
take: Best-value spot for genuine Gilgiti plates (trout, mantu, laxman) right by the river.

name: Cafe 1972
pros: Distinctive mountaineering-heritage decor (old expedition photos, wood interior)
Strong signature 1972 karahi and herbal teas
Comfortable indoor cafe experience
cons: Cuisine is mostly generic Chinese/continental, little truly local
take: Gilgit's most atmospheric cafe; go for the vibe, coffee and the house karahi rather than local specialties.

name: Dumani (Gilgit Serena Hotel)
pros: Highest hygiene and cooking standard in Gilgit
Lavish breakfast/lunch/dinner buffets with garden-valley views
Widely praised grilled trout
cons: Most expensive option in the city
Buffet skews international; less street-level local character
take: The reliable premium choice; worth it for the buffet, trout and Serena setting if budget allows.

name: Mawaid
pros: Signature tawa chicken and charcoal grills widely praised
Serves yak karahi, a genuine GB highland specialty
Good ambiance for families
take: Local go-to for tawa chicken and mixed grill; the yak karahi is a rare authentic GB dish worth ordering.

name: Pizza King GB
must_try: Chicken tikka / malai boti pizza; zinger burger
pros: Most popular pizza/fast-food chain in GB with delivery
Reasonable deals; tikka and malai boti pizzas well liked
Reliable family-friendly option
cons: Recent complaints of undersized pizzas and cold delivery
take: The default fast-food fix in Gilgit; fine for families and delivery, not for local flavor.

name: Pakiza (Hotel & Restaurant)
pros: Affordable, filling desi lunches popular with working locals
Clean dining area, indoor and outdoor seating
Central and convenient
cons: Standard Pakistani fare, no local specialty
take: Solid budget lunch stop in the city center; value over atmosphere.

name: Paradise Hotel & Restaurant
pros: Long-running riverside spot with big local following
Serves genuine chapshuro and trout karahi
Cheap and central
take: Reliable for cheap local chapshuro and river views, but quality is hit-or-miss now.

name: Indus Hotel & Restaurant
pros: Rooftop dining with mountain and river views
Cooperative staff, comfortable ambiance
Decent range of local and Pakistani dishes
cons: Cooking is solid but not distinctive
take: Pleasant rooftop option for a relaxed Pakistani meal; steady but not a headliner.

name: Sivana
pros: Riverside terrace with sunset views on Food Street
Quick, friendly service and clean kitchen
Good Shinwari mutton karahi and mixed menu
take: Pleasant riverside all-rounder on Food Street; the mutton karahi is the pick.

name: GB Steakhouse
best_for: steaks / a break from desi food / families
pros: Effectively the only proper steakhouse in Gilgit
Praised beef steaks and burgers, quality halal meat
Separate family spaces and ample parking
cons: Mixed reports of cold or inconsistent food (some raw-chicken complaints)
take: Added: the go-to when you want a Western steak/burger; stick to the steaks and it delivers.

name: Dera Shinwari Gilgit
pros: Newer 2025 arrival already ranked among Gilgit's top few
Charsi lamb karahi, Kabuli pulao and BBQ praised as excellent
Authentic Shinwari cooking, a distinct alternative to hotel dining
cons: Very new with limited review history
take: Added: hot newcomer for Shinwari charsi karahi and BBQ; strong early buzz, worth trying.
